text: Long ago, across the Red Sea from Arabia, there was a green land of high mountains called Abyssinia. Today we call it Ethiopia and Eritrea.
A girl called Barakah came from there, across the sea, to the town of Makkah. Barakah means blessing.
Help Barakah's boat cross the sea to Arabia.
In Makkah she lived in the house of a young man called Abdullah. She was not free: she had to work for his family.
Abdullah married a kind young woman called Amina. But soon Abdullah went away on a journey, and he died, far from home.
Where did Barakah come from?
From Abyssinia, across the sea
From the next street
Barakah came from Abyssinia, across the sea.
Then Amina had a baby boy. He was called Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.
Barakah loved the baby. She helped his mother look after him, by day and by night.
Rock the cradle gently. Press and hold, until he is fast asleep.
When his father died, he left five camels, some sheep, and Barakah, who looked after the baby.
Count the five camels. Tap each one.
Who helped Amina look after baby Muhammad?
Nobody at all
Barakah
Barakah helped his mother look after him, by day and by night.
When he was six, his mother took him to visit her family in the town of Yathrib, which later was called Madina. Barakah went with them, on two camels.
They stayed a whole month with his mother's family, among the date palms.
Many years later, the Prophet remembered that month. He said that he learned to swim in a pond there, and flew pigeons with the boys.
Count the pigeons! Tap each one.
Find the pairs! Things they saw in Madina.
On the way home, at a place called al-Abwa, his mother Amina fell ill.
And there, Amina died. Barakah stayed close to the little boy, and they were sad together.
Then Barakah brought him home to Makkah, on the two camels.
Help Barakah bring him home to Makkah.
Allah says to the Prophet in the Qur'an: Did He not find you an orphan and shelter you?
Who brought the little boy home to Makkah?
Barakah, on the camels
He walked home alone
Barakah brought him home, on the two camels.
In Makkah, his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib looked after him. He was a great old man of Makkah.
He said to Barakah: O blessed one! Look after this son of mine, and never forget him.
What did the grandfather call Barakah?
O lazy one
O blessed one
He called her: O blessed one. That is what Barakah means.
But when the boy was eight, his grandfather died too. Barakah saw the boy crying as he walked behind him.
Then his uncle Abu Talib took him into his home, and loved him like his own son.
Who looked after him, one after the other? Put them in order.
First, his mother Amina, with Barakah.
Then his grandfather, Abd al-Muttalib.
Then his uncle, Abu Talib.
Listen again, and put them in order.
The boy grew up into a good and honest young man. When he married Khadijah, he set Barakah free.
She married a good man called Ubayd, and they had a son called Ayman. So people called her Umm Ayman: the mother of Ayman.
The Prophet loved her very much. He used to call her: O mother!
It is told that he said: whoever would like to marry a woman of Paradise, let him marry Umm Ayman.
Some years later, when her first marriage had ended, she married Zayd, a man the Prophet loved very much. They had a son too, called Usamah.
What does each name mean? Match them.
Barakah
Blessing
Umm Ayman
The mother of Ayman
Usamah
Son of Zayd and Umm Ayman
Many people in Makkah were cruel to the Muslims. So Allah let the Muslims move to Madina, far to the north.
Umm Ayman set out too, on the long, hot road to Madina.
She was fasting, and she grew very thirsty. And she had no water.
Be patient, like Umm Ayman. Press and hold.
It is told that a bucket of cool water came down from the sky. She drank, and after that she was never thirsty again, even when she fasted on a hot day.
Catch the cool drops of water!
At last she reached Madina, with its green date palms and its kind people.
Umm Ayman was brave and kind. When the Muslims had to defend Madina, at the mountain of Uhud, she went too.
She carried water to the thirsty, and she cared for the people who were hurt.
Give everyone water. Tap each cup.
She went with the Muslims to Khaybar too, to help.
What did Umm Ayman bring to the people who were hurt?
Water
Toys
She brought them water, and she cared for them.
In Madina, the Prophet gave Umm Ayman some date palms of her own.
Later the palms had to go back to the family who had lent them. A boy called Anas came to ask for them.
But Umm Ayman said: No! He gave them to me! The Prophet offered her other trees instead. She still said no!
So he kept offering her more, until she had about ten times as many! Then she was happy.
Count her new palm trees! Tap all ten.
Once she asked him for a camel to ride. He smiled and said: I will give you the baby of a camel! She said: but a baby camel cannot carry me!
He said he would give her the baby of a camel. What did he mean?
A tiny baby camel
A big grown-up camel
He was joking! Every camel, even a big one, is the baby of a mother camel.
When the Prophet's daughter Fatimah married Ali, Umm Ayman helped to get everything ready.
She packed a bed made of palm leaves, a soft leather pillow stuffed with palm fibre, and a waterskin. And she spread soft sand on the floor.
What was in Fatimah's simple new home? Sort them.
In her home
Not there
A bed of palm leaves
A golden crown
A waterskin
A big silk sofa
Soft sand on the floor
A box of jewels
Think again. Her home was very simple.
Their home was small and simple, but it was full of love.
Help make their little home strong. Tap to place every brick.
The Prophet often went to visit Umm Ayman, to see how she was.
Once she gave him a drink, and he did not take it. So she told him off, just like a mother!
Then one day, the Prophet died. Everyone in Madina was very, very sad.
Allah says in the Qur'an: Muhammad is only a messenger, before whom many messengers have been and gone.
Abu Bakr said to Umar: let us go and visit Umm Ayman, as the Prophet used to visit her.
When they came, she wept. She said: I know he is with Allah, and that is better for him. I am crying because the news from heaven has stopped coming.
And Abu Bakr and Umar cried with her.
Why did Umm Ayman cry?
The revelation had stopped
She was hungry
She cried because the revelation, the news from heaven, had stopped coming.
Tell Umm Ayman's whole story. Tap in order.
First, Barakah came from Abyssinia, across the sea.
She looked after the baby, with his mother.
She brought the little boy home to Makkah on two camels.
He set her free, and she had a family.
She carried water to the hurt.
And he gave her ten times the palm trees.
Listen again, and tell it in order.
This is the story of Umm Ayman, Barakah, the blessing. She looked after the Prophet from the day he was born, and he called her: O mother.
